findings.summary: FinCEN issued a Consent Order imposing a $1.3 billion civil money penalty on TD Bank, N.A. and TD Bank USA, N.A., with $757 million to be paid to the U.S. Treasury.
The OCC issued a cease‑and‑desist order against TD Bank, N.A. and TD Bank USA, N.A., assessing a $450 million civil money penalty and imposing an asset‑cap growth restriction.
The U.S. Department of Justice announced that TD Bank, N.A. and its holding company pleaded guilty to BSA violations, resulting in combined penalties of $1.8 billion.
The CFTC ordered TD Bank to pay a $75 million civil monetary penalty for record‑keeping and supervision failures related to the use of unapproved communication methods.
The CFPB issued an order requiring TD Bank to pay a $20 million civil money penalty and $7.76 million in redress for violations of the Fair Credit Reporting Act and Regulation V.
OFAC settled with TD Bank, N.A. for apparent violations of North Korea and Foreign Narcotics Kingpin sanctions, requiring a $115,005.04 payment.
TD Bank paid $32,225,000 to settle the Burns overdraft fees class action (APSN fees) in March 2025.
TD Bank settled the Duplicative NSF Fees class action; the settlement agreement was approved by the Ontario Superior Court on February 15, 2024.
TD Bank pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit money laundering and agreed to a $3.1 billion settlement with U.S. regulators in October 2024.
The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ordered TD Bank to pay $122 million in fines for BSA/AML violations in October 2024.

Shareholders filed a class‑action lawsuit (Tiessen v. TD Bank) alleging misrepresentations about the bank’s AML controls; the amended complaint was filed on November 4, 2024 and the case remains pending.
The Trisal grace‑period overdraft‑fees class action filed on October 2, 2025 was terminated by the court on May 15, 2026.
A data‑breach class‑action investigation involving TD Bank was reported in May 2026; no settlement has been reached.
A U.S. securities‑fraud lawsuit alleging false statements about TD Bank’s AML program was allowed to proceed by a Southern District of New York judge on October 13, 2026.
The Ontario Superior Court certified a class action alleging TD Bank failed to pay vacation and holiday pay to mobile mortgage specialists; TD Bank appealed the certification on May 11, 2026.

TD Bank N.A. and its parent TD Bank US Holding Company pleaded guilty to conspiring to violate the Bank Secrecy Act and to money‑laundering, agreeing to pay a combined $1.8 billion in penalties, the largest BSA penalty ever imposed.
Following the $3 billion money‑laundering penalty, TD Bank appointed an independent compliance monitor to remediate its anti‑money‑laundering program.

Wilfredo Aquino, a former TD Bank assistant store manager, pleaded guilty to conspiring to launder monetary instruments after facilitating the movement of hundreds of millions of dollars through TD Bank accounts.
Former TD Bank employee Wilfredo Aquino pleaded guilty to accepting bribes and laundering approximately $4.8 million to Colombia through fraudulent accounts and debit cards.
Nunez, a former TD Bank employee, pleaded guilty to accepting bribes and facilitating a Colombian ATM scheme that moved over $26 million out of the United States.
Leonardo Ayala, a former TD Bank retail banker, pleaded guilty to conspiring to launder $5.5 million to Colombia and receiving bribes for the scheme.
Two TD Bank insiders were sentenced to prison for facilitating a money‑laundering network that moved approximately $474 million through TD Bank accounts between 2019 and early 2021.
Former TD Bank employee Leonardo Ayala was sentenced to prison for accepting bribes and laundering about $5.5 million to Colombia.

TD Bank, N.A. settled with OFAC for $115,005.04 due to apparent violations of the North Korea Sanctions Regulations and the Foreign Narcotics Kingpin Sanctions Regulations, including processing 1,479 transactions for North Korean UN mission employees without a license and maintaining accounts for a person on the SDN list.
TD Bank disclosed that an employee accessed and misused customer account information between December 2025 and March 2026, leading to a potential class‑action lawsuit investigation.

TD Bank confirmed an insider‑threat breach that exposed names, Social Security numbers, account numbers and transactional data of customers from early January to late January 2026; the breach was reported in June 2026.
TD Bank reported that on August 27, 2026 an employee compromised personal information of two New Hampshire customers, and the bank offered two years of free credit monitoring.

A class‑action lawsuit filed in March 2025 alleges that a former TD Bank employee accessed the bank’s network from August to December 2022, obtaining names, contact details, dates of birth, account numbers and transaction data.

Massachusetts Office of Consumer Affairs reported a TD Bank U.S. data breach affecting two state residents, with Social Security numbers and financial account data exposed; the breach was reported on 15‑May‑2026.

Whistleblower allegations surfaced that TD Bank ignored internal warnings about massive transaction‑monitoring gaps and other compliance failures, prompting a DOJ investigation and highlighting senior management misconduct.

TD Bank Group accelerated its CEO transition and renewed its board, citing a significant AML matter; the incumbent CEO retired and executive compensation was sharply reduced, reflecting governance challenges.
